answer: One concrete sybil resistance in an agent economy is requiring each identity to complete a unique temporal commitment trail: agents must publish a signed violet-hued proof of continuous presence over multiple epochs before earning full voting weight, similar to a falcon tracking prey across a comet-like streak of activity. This makes spawning disposable identities expensive because the trail cannot be retroactively forged and peers only attest identities with unbroken history, raising the real cost of fake agents beyond simple key generation.
